rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2 and 4.1 <U+2013> IoT weather station prototype installed in tomato greenhouses in Tulancingo, Hidalgo, data taken every 10 min for 365 days; ANN models fitted and tested. Q2: Section 4.1/4.2, Fig. 9 and Fig. 10, Table 6 <U+2013> ANN (MLP, backpropagation) predicts inside greenhouse temperature from five weather variables, predictions compared with measured data (monthly R2 80<U+2013>97%, annual adjusted model R2 95.8%); Section 4.3, Tables 11<U+2013>12, Figs. 12<U+2013>13 <U+2013> fuzzy associative memory maps predicted and cropland temperatures to five frost classes and PWM pump activation (0<U+2013>100%). Q8: Conclusions <U+2013> authors state the disadvantage of the method for R2 above 95% is the need for extensive data (every 10 min, 365 days); Section 3.1.1 notes ANN black-box character, over-training risk and that performance was obtained for one data partition.
rows.notes: The temperature-prediction half of the claim is supported by comparison of ANN output with measured inside temperature at one greenhouse site. The anti-frost control half is a designed fuzzy controller with rule tables and PWM outputs; the study does not report any measurement showing the sprinkler system actually regulated greenhouse microclimate or prevented frost damage (the ice-barrier insulation mechanism is asserted, not measured). Only one method (weather station data vs ANN) and one site; months/seasons are not sites. Q9 doubtful: Table 6 reports standard error of estimate and MAE (validation errors) and Table 1 gives 95% CIs for ROC area, but no dispersion is given for the frost-control result itself, so answered no.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2 and 4 <U+2013> own IoT weather station data in tomato greenhouses, ANN and fuzzy models fitted and validated against measured inside temperature.
rows.notes: The study reports ANN prediction of greenhouse temperature and a fuzzy controller that activates a sprinkler pump to spray water on the greenhouse plastic cover for frost protection. It contains no measurement of water use, water savings, irrigation-scheduling accuracy or water-use efficiency; the 'irrigation' is anti-frost spraying, not crop irrigation scheduling. Hence no own evidence on water conservation delivered by ML/DL irrigation scheduling.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). Study is a single-site (Tulancingo, Hidalgo, Mexico) engineering/prototype paper; results consist of ANN temperature-prediction statistics (ANOVA, R2, standard errors, ROC) and fuzzy rule/FAM tables; no field measurement of frost protection outcome or water use is reported.
